appendOnly.note: Nothing sealed is edited. The predecessor plan keeps its bytes, the two superseded source files stay in the tree at their sealed digests, and the guest-init contract keeps the clause this record disagrees with. Succession is by new file only.

supersessions.what: the launcher unit with its output also going to the console
supersessions.why: the sealed boot receipt records that where the launcher refuses was not observable. Two lines change: standard output and standard error each gain the console alongside the journal. The console is a channel the host already captures and hashes, so this adds no device, no network and no shared directory. Every other line, including the capability set and the account the unit runs as, is byte-identical to v1.

supersessions.what: the runtime directory rules, with the three that cannot succeed removed
supersessions.why: v1 asks for three directories under /var/lib/boole on a filesystem mounted read-only. Those three lines cannot succeed and were never going to. Removing them makes the condition that every write lands on tmpfs true by construction rather than true because the failures happened to be harmless. The two lines that remain are both under /run, which is tmpfs. The launcher's lock and socket live there and nowhere else. Nothing the launcher needs was under /var/lib/boole: the replay node unit is the only thing that names node-state, and that unit is not staged into this image.

discrepancyFound.correctedHere: This plan records the audited image as the fact and the contract clause as the stale half. The contract is not edited: four authority records name it at its sealed digest.
discrepancyFound.earlierStatement: filesystemLayout.writableMounts lists /var/lib/boole as a tmpfs mounted at every boot
discrepancyFound.howItWasChecked: The mount table was decoded from the relocated read-only data of the libsystemd-shared the image ships, and the seven mount units in the image were read directly. No fstab is present, so no generator adds one. Five top-level paths are mounted: /dev, /proc, /run, /sys and /tmp. /var is not among them and nothing sits below /var in either list.
discrepancyFound.whatTheAuditShows: No such mount exists in the image that booted. Nothing is mounted over /var, so a tree staged under /var/lib/boole is neither masked nor made writable.
discrepancyFound.whyItMatters: Both halves of the runtime-rootfs gap depend on it. If /var/lib/boole were a tmpfs, a baked tree there would be hidden at boot and the launcher's read-only check would fail on the writable mount. Neither happens.

modeRationale.note: The three files anything reads are world-readable. The two that carry password fields are readable by root alone. Ubuntu gives the password files to a shadow group; this image has no shadow group and no process that would join it, so the narrower mode is the honest one.

perFile./etc/group: read twice by the identity contract, by name and by number
perFile./etc/gshadow: the same reason as the password file it accompanies
perFile./etc/nsswitch.conf: glibc reads it in every process that resolves a name
perFile./etc/passwd: the identity contract reads it and nothing writes it
perFile./etc/shadow: no process below root has any reason to read a password file

whereTheDigestIsAlreadySealed.how: compiled into the sealed launcher as RUNTIME_ROOTFS_CONTENT_MANIFEST_SHA256

contentManifest.whyItIsNotATrackedSourceRow: The closure plan expected one tracked-file row for it. A tracked row would mean committing 1,285,116 bytes of build output as though they were a source, and the builder already emits this document from the entries it assembled. Deriving it from the nested assembly and requiring the derived digest to equal the value the launcher compiles against is the same check with one fewer copy of the same bytes.

drivenBy.whyNotTheBootLock: The manifest records each entry's closure names. Assembled from the boot lock the closure names would be the boot lock's five, and the document would not match the digest the launcher compiles against. The nested assembly is therefore driven by the runtime lock, whose artifacts the boot lock already carries in full.

whyTheReadOnlyCheckPasses.launcherRequires: fstatvfs on the opened directory reports ST_RDONLY
whyTheReadOnlyCheckPasses.note: The launcher opens the prefix and refuses unless the filesystem under it is mounted read-only. The root disk is mounted read-only and nothing is mounted over /var, so the check is answered by the root mount itself rather than by a mount added for it.

packageSelection.canonicalOrdering: packages sorted by packageId, artifacts sorted by id, seeds and seed package IDs sorted and unique
packageSelection.sourceOfTruth: every package row must be byte-identical to the verified dependency candidate closure and must appear in the payload acquisition result

predecessor.whatItStillGoverns: the boot source lock that already exists, and every record that pins that lock. This successor governs a lock that has not been generated.

successorChainPosition.note: The order is fixed because each step is the input the next one checks against. This record is the first, and it produces no lock, no builder change and no image.

theBudgets.note: Both are upper bounds read back from sealed records rather than counts of an assembled tree. Neither is evidence that the tree fits; both say a tree of this shape has room. The measurement that decides is taken immediately before assembly.
